02

Three Exposures for Operators

I

Age Verification Is Now an Engineering Problem With a Legal Deadline.

The Child Digital Safety Law requires active filtering and age verification, which in practice means AI-driven moderation. That deployment is an AI system under governance. Has anyone treated it as one?

II

Your Suppliers Are About to Be Filtered.

NCAP will restrict which providers may serve critical infrastructure. The review only means something if it comes from outside the supplier base. Consider who would carry it out if you commissioned it tomorrow.

III

Your Fintech Arm Is Regulated Even If the Group Is Not.

Operator-owned wallets and payment businesses sit under CBUAE supervision with management liability attached. That obligation frequently sits outside the network security team’s remit, and outside its visibility.

04

Common Questions

What does the Child Digital Safety Law require of ISPs?

Active content filtering and age verification since January 2026, which in practice means AI-driven moderation inside AI-governance scope.

Will NCAP affect which security vendors we can use?

It is expected to — providers serving critical infrastructure will need UAE accreditation, so suppliers without it cannot hold those roles.

Does the TDRA require subscriber data to stay in the UAE?

Regulated data is subject to in-country residency expectations, and the practical question is which vendor platforms process it on your behalf.

How do you assess change attribution on a control plane?

Within the network trust review, we reconstruct a real change end to end, from request through approval to execution, and measure how long the answer takes to assemble.

Do you provide monitoring and incident response?

Yes, through our Managed Detection & Response service: 24/7 monitoring and response on an annual term. Your network operations stay with your team. In markets that require a license, operations run through a licensed partner named in the contract.
